_comment: R3-06 claims-audit wave, probes for batches 8-10 (15 skills, 68 contradicted claims; the first batches written with the mechanical sweep). One probe per contradicted-claim class. Arm A = model alone, arm B = model + the owning skill's SKILL.md + llm-anti-patterns.md (run_lift). Quotes are verbatim lines from scratchpad/corpus264 (264) or scratchpad/corpus (262). Built 2026-10-20.

probes.question: What access levels can a guest user sharing rule grant on an Experience Cloud site?
probes.wrong_answer: Read, Read/Write, or Read/Write/Transfer, like any criteria-based sharing rule.
probes.correct_answer: Read Only only. Guest user sharing rules cannot grant edit access.
probes.quote: Guest user sharing rules can only grant Read Only access.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: guests could update records via a sharing rule

probes.question: Can an admin turn off the Secure Guest User Record Access setting (enableSecureGuestAccess) in a current org?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes, it is a toggle that can be disabled to restore the old guest sharing model.
probes.correct_answer: No. As of API version 50.0 the field's value is always true regardless of what you set.
probes.quote: As of API version 50.0, this field's value is always true, regardless of
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'does not retroactively migrate', implying it is optional

probes.question: In Visualforce, what is JSINHTMLENCODE(x) equivalent to, and in which order are the two encodings applied?
probes.wrong_answer: HTMLENCODE(JSENCODE(x)): JavaScript encoding first, then HTML.
probes.correct_answer: JSENCODE(HTMLENCODE(x)): it first encodes with HTMLENCODE, then encodes that result with JSENCODE.
probes.quote: That is, JSINHTMLENCODE first encodes someValue with HTMLENCODE, and then encodes the result with JSENCODE.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'JS first, then HTML'

probes.question: Does a custom Visualforce page automatically get the org's Content Security Policy restricting it to trusted URLs?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes, the org CSP applies to all Visualforce pages and the default is restrictive.
probes.correct_answer: No. For custom Visualforce pages, content is restricted to trusted URLs only if the page's cspHeader attribute is set to true.
probes.quote: URLs only if the page’s cspHeader attribute is set to true.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'subject to the org CSP / default is restrictive'

probes.question: What modifiers must an Apex method carry to be callable through JavaScript remoting in Visualforce?
probes.wrong_answer: Any public instance method annotated @RemoteAction works.
probes.correct_answer: It must be static and either global or public, with the @RemoteAction annotation; there is no <apex:remoteAction> component.
probes.quote: Methods with the RemoteAction annotation must be static and either global or public.

probes.question: If a Shield Platform Encryption tenant secret is destroyed, is the data encrypted with it lost forever?
probes.wrong_answer: Yes, destroying a tenant secret is irreversible and the data is permanently unreadable.
probes.correct_answer: Not necessarily: the data is inaccessible unless you previously exported the key and import it back into Salesforce.
probes.quote: tenant secret, related data isn’t accessible unless you previously exported the key and then import the key back into Salesforce
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'destroying a tenant secret is irreversible'

probes.question: When you enable Shield Platform Encryption on a field that already holds data, does the existing data get encrypted?
probes.wrong_answer: No, the policy encrypts only new writes; existing records stay plaintext until you run a re-encryption job yourself.
probes.correct_answer: Yes. A background encryption process applies the active key material to existing data; field history and feed tracking values are included when enableEncryptFieldHistory is true.
probes.quote: Indicates whether the background encryption process applies the
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: 'policy encrypts only new writes; run a re-encryption job'

probes.question: When a permission set assignment with an ExpirationDate reaches that date, what happens to the permissions?
probes.wrong_answer: Nothing automatic; an admin must remove the assignment by hand.
probes.correct_answer: The added permissions are revoked at the timestamp in PermissionSetAssignment.ExpirationDate.
probes.wrong_source: skill before audit: the revocation at expiry was marked unverifiable
